coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 11
record.summary: Planned office building on the Potrero Power Station masterplan (office, laboratory and life science uses are permitted there), paired with Block 12 (the project's engineer describes the two together as about 430,000 sq ft of office, while the Planning Department's October 2020 Phase 1 approval lists about 219,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 11 and 177,000 for Block 12); design was under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report. In a request reported July 29, 2026, the developer asked to raise Block 11's height by 15 feet; the Planning Commission approved the amendment unanimously (reported Aug 3, 2026) and the Board of Supervisors passed the amended development agreement on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (enactment is not confirmed). No construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is Assessor lot 4232021, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. That this is the lot of Block 11 is Pier & Point's own inference from location, shape and size (our earlier trace of the D4D figure measured 2,908 m2 against the lot's 2,776 m2; 77% of the trace lies inside the lot and the trace covers 81% of it). No document read ties the lot number to it. A building may sit back from the lot lines. Block 11 is not yet built (design under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lot 4232021 (recorded 2022-08-30; mapped 2023-12-01; active); cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: No single Assessor lot is documented as Block 11. Lot 4232021 (active) matches its location, shape and size, so its outline is Assessor lot 4232021; the identification is Pier & Point's inference, as the accuracy note says.
notes.regulatory_context: Flat 130 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D (the colour-coded height label). The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) shows Non-Retail Sales and Services (including office), Laboratory and Life Science uses permitted (subject to the table's note 13) and Residential not permitted here. Blocks 11 and 12 together are described as approximately 430,000 sq ft of office by the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+ Engineers project page, a consultant's own material, not a Planning document). The Meyers+ page and the June 7, 2020 pre-application community meeting slides list Herzog & de Meuron + Adamson Associates as architect for Blocks 11, 12 and 15. No construction-start source found.

facts.value: Non-Retail Sales/Services (office) and Laboratory/Life Science uses permitted; Residential Not Permitted (D4D final Table 3.1.1)

Blocks 11 and 12 combined: approximately 430,000 sq ft of office, with below-grade parking, per the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+). The Oct 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists Block 11 at approximately 219,000 sq ft of commercial (plus 5,000 retail, 6,000 PDR, 6,000 childcare and about 48,500 accessory parking) and Block 12 at approximately 177,000 sq ft of commercial (about 396,000 commercial together); the two sources differ and no source reconciles them

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement covering the adopted Design for Development, whose Land Use Table (Table 3.1.1) lists Block 11 as a development block; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date. open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 11; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+). The Planning Department's October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists approximately 219,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 11 and 177,000 for Block 12 (about 396,000 together, plus retail, PDR, childcare and other uses); no source reconciles the two figures.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +15 ft height increase is tied to the Development Agreement and Planning Code amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026; Legistar lists 'Final action: 10/6/2026' and status 'Mayors Office' with the enactment date and number blank (page read Oct 12, 2026), so it is not confirmed as enacted and this record's height fact still shows the adopted limit.

This record's map outline is DataSF Assessor lot 4232021 (active, unaddressed, recorded 2022-08-30), chosen because 77% of our earlier trace of the D4D figure lies inside it; that this lot is Block 11's own parcel is an inference from location, shape and size, and no document read names the lot.
